key_insight: The paper introduces a faster normal-form algorithm for Pauli-LIMDDs that reduces the worst-case cost from O(n^3) to O(n^2) when a node has one child, preserving O(n^3) for two distinct children.
engineering_relevance: This improves the practicality of quantum-circuit simulation by making LIMDD-based tools faster and more capable on Clifford and some high-T-count circuits.
method: Derive a new normal-form procedure for Pauli-LIMDD nodes.
Exploit equivalence merging to handle single-child nodes more efficiently.
Implement the algorithm from scratch in C/C++ within QolDDer.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that QolDDer matches the theoretical advantages of Pauli-LIMDDs, is significantly faster than existing LIMDD simulators on Clifford circuits, and often outperforms them by an order of magnitude on a public quantum-circuit dataset.
watch_item: The speedup is strongest for single-child nodes; the two-distinct-children case still has O(n^3) complexity, so gains may depend on circuit structure and implementation quality.
paper_title: Faster algorithm for achieving minimal-size quantum decision diagrams
